formula: Target Word Class = Option Word Class (Noun ➔ Noun | Verb ➔ Verb | Adj ➔ Adj | Adv ➔ Adv)
auxiliary: Mandatory Part-of-Speech Alignment (never accept a noun for an adjective)
usage: Synonym ya Antonym hamesha same grammatical category se belong karna chahiye. Agar target word Adjective hai, toh option mein Noun ya Verb aane par use bina padhe foran eliminate karein. Examiner candidates ko distract karne ke liye word-family ke doosre parts of speech options mein daalta hai.
keyTip: POS FILTER FIRST: Kisi bhi option ko test karne se pehle uska Part of Speech verify karein. Agar question mein 'generous' (adjective) hai, toh 'generosity' (noun) dekhte hi eliminate kar dein.

formula: Read Sentence Context ➔ Freeze Active Word Sense ➔ Match Candidate to Active Sense
auxiliary: Discard candidate options matching secondary dictionary senses
usage: English mein ek word ke multiple meanings (polysemy) ho sakte hain. Sentence-based question mein examiner target word ke secondary sense ka popular synonym option mein rakhta hai taaki careless students fas sakein. Sentence ke context se pehle active sense ko lock karein.

patterns.affirmative: Legal/Rational Sense: "The judge delivered a SOUND judgment." ➔ Valid / Solid / Robust (NOT: *noise)
patterns.negative: Critical/Serious Sense: "The forged stamp is a GRAVE matter." ➔ Serious / Critical (NOT: *tomb)
patterns.interrogative: Clarity Sense: "The PLAIN statutory wording is binding." ➔ Clear / Evident (NOT: *flat land)

keyTip: FALSE SENSE ELIMINATION: Agar word 'grave' hai aur sentence mein 'grave mistake' likha hai, toh 'tomb' ya 'burial' option secondary trap hai; 'serious' hi correct answer hai.

tense: Gradable Scale Opposites vs Intermediate Degrees
formula: Target Scale Extreme <=====> Antonym Scale Extreme (Exclude Weaker / Milder Points)
auxiliary: Milder degree is NOT an antonym (Warm is a weak degree, not an opposite of Hot)
usage: Gradable adjectives ek continuous continuum par exist karte hain. Kisi extreme word ka antonym doosre extreme par hona chahiye. Us continuum ke intermediate ya weaker points antonyms nahi kehlate.

patterns.affirmative: Temperature Continuum: Hot <--> Cold (Warm and Cool are intermediate shades, NOT antonyms of Hot)
patterns.negative: Size Continuum: Immense / Colossal <--> Tiny / Minute (Small is a weaker synonym of Tiny)
patterns.interrogative: Anger Continuum: Furious / Enraged <--> Calm / Serene (Annoyed is a mild degree of Anger)

keyTip: EXTREME TO EXTREME: Extreme intensity wale word ka opposite hamesha extreme opposite hoga. 'Furious' ka antonym 'Calm' hoga, na ki 'Annoyed'.

formula: State A IS TRUE <=====> State B IS FALSE (Zero Intermediate State)
auxiliary: Strict mutual exclusivity: there is no middle ground between complementary pairs
usage: Complementary antonyms mutually exclusive hote hain. Agar koi entity State A mein hai, toh wo State B mein nahi ho sakti, aur koi beech ka vikalp sambhav nahi hai.

patterns.affirmative: Biological Status: Alive <--> Dead (Zero middle state; one cannot be 'slightly dead')
patterns.negative: Judicial Status: Valid <--> Void (A statutory order is either legally valid or null/void)
patterns.interrogative: Marital/Legal Status: Single <--> Married | Pass <--> Fail | Present <--> Absent

keyTip: COMPLEMENTARY TEST: Complementary opposites mein 'more' ya 'very' nahi lag sakta—*very dead ya *more married bolna grammatically invalid hai.

formula: Entity 1 Relation to Entity 2 <=====> Entity 2 Converse Relation to Entity 1
auxiliary: Perspective shifts describe the same relationship from opposite points of view
usage: Converse ya relational antonyms kisi single relationship ko do opposing perspectives se describe karte hain. Inme scale ya polarity nahi hoti, balki mutual role-exchange hota hai.

patterns.affirmative: Transactional: Buy <--> Sell | Lend <--> Borrow | Pay <--> Receive
patterns.negative: Hierarchical/Social: Employer <--> Employee | Teacher <--> Student | Landlord <--> Tenant
patterns.interrogative: Spatial/Relational: Above <--> Below | Predecessor <--> Successor | Parent <--> Child

keyTip: RECIPROCAL ROLES: Agar A ne B ko paisa diya, toh A ne 'lend' kiya aur B ne 'borrow' kiya. Ye dono verbs mutually relational antonyms hain.

formula: Target Intensity Rank (Level 1 to 5) = Synonym Intensity Rank (Level 1 to 5)
auxiliary: Never substitute an extreme intensity word with a mild word
usage: Synonyms choose karte waqt emotional force aur semantic degree match hona anivarya hai. Ek mild approval word extreme adoration word ka synonym nahi ban sakta.

patterns.affirmative: Dislike Continuum: Dislike (Mild) ➔ Resent (Medium) ➔ Detest / Loathe / Abhor (Extreme)
patterns.negative: Happy Continuum: Content (Mild) ➔ Glad / Happy (Standard) ➔ Ecstatic / Jubilant (Extreme)
patterns.interrogative: Fear Continuum: Apprehensive (Mild) ➔ Afraid (Standard) ➔ Terrified / Petrified (Extreme)

keyTip: INTENSITY MATCH: Agar target word 'Abhor' (Extreme hatred) hai, toh 'Dislike' (Mild) galat distractor hai; 'Loathe' ya 'Detest' hi accurate answer hai.

formula: Target Word Valence (+ / - / Neutral) = Synonym Valence (+ / - / Neutral)
auxiliary: Positive praise cannot be synonymous with negative mockery
usage: Kayi words identical denotation (core meaning) share karte hain lekin unka emotional charge (connotation) vipreet hota hai. Synonym ka tone target word ke tone ke sath 100% align hona chahiye.

patterns.affirmative: Determination: Resolute / Tenacious (Positive) vs Stubborn / Obstinate (Negative/Pejorative)
patterns.negative: Frugality: Thrifty / Economical (Commendatory) vs Miserly / Stingy (Pejorative)
patterns.interrogative: Confidence: Confident / Bold (Positive) vs Arrogant / Presptuous (Negative)

keyTip: VALENCE CHECK: Context check karein: kya speaker tareef kar raha hai ya aalochana? Agar sentence tareef kar raha hai, toh 'stubborn' jaisa negative word kabhi synonym nahi banega.

formula: im- [before p, b, m] | il- [before l] | ir- [before r] | in- [default before vowels/others]
auxiliary: Pronunciation ease governs the negative Latin prefix form
usage: Latin prefix 'in-' different initial consonants ke aage phonetically transform ho jata hai. Is rule ko samajhne se exam mein wrong-spelling wale distractors foran pehchane ja sakte hain.

patterns.affirmative: Bilabial Consonants (p, b, m): in- + prudent ➔ Imprudent | in- + mortal ➔ Immortal
patterns.negative: Liquid Consonant (l): in- + legal ➔ Illegal | in- + literate ➔ Illiterate | in- + logical ➔ Illogical
patterns.interrogative: Rhotic Consonant (r): in- + regular ➔ Irregular | in- + relevant ➔ Irrelevant | in- + resolute ➔ Irresolute

keyTip: SPELLING IMMUNITY: Kabhi bhi *unlegal ya *inregular choose na karein. 'L' ke aage 'il-' aur 'R' ke aage 'ir-' ka phonetic law hamesha govern karta hai.

formula: Invaluable = Extremely Valuable | Inflammable = Flammable | Disinterested = Impartial
auxiliary: Do NOT treat 'in-' or 'dis-' as standard negatives in these three classic trap words
usage: Kuch words mein negative prefix laga hota hai lekin unka meaning ordinary negative nahi hota. Examiners in teen words par repeated questions banate hain.

patterns.affirmative: Invaluable: 'Value cannot be measured because it is so high' ➔ Priceless (Antonym: Worthless)
patterns.negative: Inflammable: 'In- + flame + able = catches fire easily' ➔ Flammable (Antonym: Non-flammable)
patterns.interrogative: Disinterested: 'Free from self-interest' ➔ Impartial / Unbiased (NOT: *Uninterested = bored)

keyTip: CLASSIC TRAP SHIELD: Agar exam mein 'Invaluable' ka antonym pucha jaye, toh 'Valuable' tick mat karna; iska antonym 'Worthless' ya 'Valueless' hota hai.

formula: Exclude Option IF Suffix Indicates Differing Grammatical Class (-ity, -ness, -ly, -tion)
auxiliary: A noun ending in -ence/-ance cannot serve as a synonym for an adjective ending in -ent/-ant
usage: Examiners question word ke hi word-family ke doosre derivatives options mein daalte hain taaki hurried students confused ho jayein. Suffixes ke zariye unka POS check karein.

patterns.affirmative: Adjective Target: Diligent (Adj) ➔ Industrious (Adj) | Exclude: Diligence (Noun)
patterns.negative: Noun Target: Adversity (Noun) ➔ Hardship (Noun) | Exclude: Adverse (Adj), Adversely (Adv)
patterns.interrogative: Verb Target: Exonerate (Verb) ➔ Acquit (Verb) | Exclude: Exoneration (Noun)

keyTip: SUFFIX CHECK: Noun suffixes (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity) aur Adjective suffixes (-able, -ous, -ent, -ic) se option ka POS turant pehchan kar eliminate karein.

formula: Select Candidate Matching Natural Domain Collocations (Legal / Formal / Administrative)
auxiliary: A word may be a dictionary synonym, but if it sounds unnatural in the sentence domain, reject it
usage: Dictionary synonyms hamesha sentence ke domain ke sath collocate nahi karte. Legal judgments, statutory orders, aur high court pleadings formal register demand karte hain.

patterns.affirmative: Court Context: The magistrate QUASHED the charge sheet. (NOT: *canceled, *suppressed)
patterns.negative: Statutory Context: The Governor PROMULGATED the ordinance. (NOT: *broadcast, *published)
patterns.interrogative: Evidence Context: The prosecution ADDUCED fresh evidence. (NOT: *brought, *supplied)

keyTip: FORMAL REGISTER: Informal conversational words ('put off', 'start', 'show') ko official judicial contexts mein eliminate karein aur unke formal equivalents ('adjourn', 'commence', 'adduce') ko chunein.

formula: Step 1 Polarity ➔ Step 2 POS ➔ Step 3 Context Sense ➔ Step 4 Tone ➔ Step 5 Intensity
auxiliary: Execute all 5 filters sequentially; never guess based on surface familiarity
usage: High Court examination hall mein 100% accuracy hasil karne ke liye har vocabulary question par ye rigid 5-step checklist execute karein.

patterns.affirmative: Step 1: Check Prompt (Synonym vs Antonym underline karein)
patterns.negative: Step 2 & 3: POS match karein aur sentence context se active sense freeze karein
patterns.interrogative: Step 4 & 5: Connotation (+ / -) aur intensity degree verify karke correct option lock karein

keyTip: UNDERLINE PROMPT FIRST: Sabse pehla kaam question mein 'SYNONYM' ya 'ANTONYM' ko underline karna hai. Is aadat se aapke 2 marks free mein bach jayenge.
